items.prompt: An overhead camera sees a floor marker at camera-frame coordinates (X, Y, Z) = (0.1, -0.1, 2) m. Camera axes: x right, y down, z forward along the optical axis (Z is depth). Image axes: u grows to the right and v grows downward from the top-left pixel. Intrinsics: fx=400 px, fy=420 px, principal point (cx, cy) = (320, 240) px; no distortion. Compute the pixel coordinates (u, v), graded within ±0.001 px.
items.solution: u = fx·X/Z + cx = 400·0.1/2 + 320 = 340 px; v = fy·Y/Z + cy = 420·(-0.1)/2 + 240 = 219 px. Swapping fx and fy would give (341, 220); a y-up image convention would give v = 261. The supplied calibration is assumed, not estimated.
hints: The marker is slightly right of the optical axis (X > 0) and slightly above it (Y < 0 with y down), so expect u a little above cx and v a little below cy.
Normalise by depth first: X/Z = 0.05 and Y/Z = -0.05. Next multiply each by its own focal length (fx for u, fy for v) and add the principal point.

u = fx·X/Z + cx = 400·0.1/2 + 320 = 340 px; v = fy·Y/Z + cy = 420·(-0.1)/2 + 240 = 219 px. Swapping fx and fy would give (341, 220); a y-up image convention would give v = 261. The supplied calibration is assumed, not estimated.
items.remediation: If you got (341, 220) you swapped fx and fy; v = 261 means you flipped the image y axis. Revisit /lessons/V03.

items.prompt: A wrist camera sees a point at camera-frame coordinates (X, Y, Z) = (-0.2, 0.15, 0.75) m. Camera axes: x right, y down, z forward along the optical axis (Z is depth). Image axes: u grows to the right and v grows downward from the top-left pixel. Intrinsics: fx=300 px, fy=500 px, principal point (cx, cy) = (160, 120) px; no distortion. Compute the pixel coordinates (u, v), graded within ±0.001 px.
items.solution: u = fx·X/Z + cx = 300·(-0.2)/0.75 + 160 = 80 px; v = fy·Y/Z + cy = 500·0.15/0.75 + 120 = 220 px. Swapping fx and fy would give (26.667, 180); a y-up image convention would give v = 20. The supplied calibration is assumed, not estimated.
hints: The point is left of the optical axis (X < 0) and below it (Y > 0 with y down), close to the camera; the focal lengths for u and v differ a lot.
Normalise by depth first: X/Z = -0.2/0.75 ≈ -0.266667 and Y/Z = 0.2. Next multiply each by its own focal length (fx for u, fy for v) and add the principal point.

u = fx·X/Z + cx = 300·(-0.2)/0.75 + 160 = 80 px; v = fy·Y/Z + cy = 500·0.15/0.75 + 120 = 220 px. Swapping fx and fy would give (26.667, 180); a y-up image convention would give v = 20. The supplied calibration is assumed, not estimated.
items.remediation: If you got (26.667, 180) you swapped fx and fy; v = 20 means you flipped the image y axis. Revisit /lessons/V03.

items.prompt: A wrist camera's rangefinder reports a point 1.3 m from the camera centre (Euclidean range). Its camera-frame coordinates are (X, Y, Z) = (-0.3, 0.4, 1.2) m. Camera axes: x right, y down, z forward along the optical axis (Z is depth). Image axes: u grows to the right and v grows downward from the top-left pixel. Intrinsics: fx=300 px, fy=480 px, principal point (cx, cy) = (160, 120) px; no distortion. Compute the pixel coordinates (u, v), graded within ±0.001 px.
items.solution: u = fx·X/Z + cx = 300·(-0.3)/1.2 + 160 = 85 px; v = fy·Y/Z + cy = 480·0.4/1.2 + 120 = 280 px. Z = 1.2 m is the depth; dividing by the range 1.3 m instead would give u = 90.769 px. The supplied calibration is assumed, not estimated.
hints: Two distances are given; only one of them is the depth Z along the optical axis that the pinhole model divides by.
Normalise by depth first: X/Z = -0.25 and Y/Z = 0.4/1.2 ≈ 0.333333. Next multiply each by its own focal length (fx for u, fy for v) and add the principal point.

u = fx·X/Z + cx = 300·(-0.3)/1.2 + 160 = 85 px; v = fy·Y/Z + cy = 480·0.4/1.2 + 120 = 280 px. Z = 1.2 m is the depth; dividing by the range 1.3 m instead would give u = 90.769 px. The supplied calibration is assumed, not estimated.
items.remediation: If you got u about 90.769 you divided by the range instead of the depth Z. Swapping fx and fy gives (40, 220). Revisit /lessons/V03.
